thread:
Ash: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a 'release conductor' flow to wrap the usual deploy-bot steps into one command. Thinking shortcuts + hooks + a small template for release notes.
Jamie: nice. what do you want the primary command shape to be?
Ash: something like `/conductor start --service payments --pin v2.3.1 --canary 5 --window '2026-03-21T15:00Z/1h' --notes-template quick`
Sophie: love that. can the conductor auto-create the release note in JIRA/GH release?
Ash: yes, intend to have `--publish-release` flag that posts generated notes and links. also `--dry-run` to preview preflight checks.
Alex: for rollbacks, we should expose `--safe-rollback` that runs health checks and optionally cancels if errors spike. also an escape hatch like `/conductor rollback --to=prev --reason 'hotfix regress'`
release-bot: :robot_face: available actions: start, promote, snapshot, rollback, finalize. run `/conductor help` for usage.
Jamie: can we include hook points for preflight and postmortem scripts? e.g., `--pre-hook 'scripts/check-schema.sh'` and `--post-hook 'scripts/notify-on-call.sh'`
Ash: yes. also want templated checklist output that shows required approvals, pin status, and quick links. sample output: ```
Release checklist for payments v2.3.1
- Pin: v2.3.1 (ok)
- Canary: 5% -> 50% timeline: 10m/30m
- Preflight checks: lint, smoke, infra
- Approvals: qa, security
- Change window: 2026-03-21T15:00Z -> 1h
- Hooks: pre-hook.sh, post-hook.sh
```
Sophie: can the conductor intelligently choose routes? e.g., if dedicated capacity low, fallback to host variant and annotate cost delta.
Alex: add `--route-policy prefer-dedicated, fallback-hosted` and `--cost-guard max-increase=1.2`
Oliver: small UX ask — when invoking from Slack, support a modal that fills the fields and shows the generated release note text before confirm. and a compact summary message after start with `Pin`, `Canary`, `ETA` and a `Rollback` button.
Ash: agreed. Slack modal and a persistent thread that the team can use to annotate incidents. also store the conductor run id for audit. example quick commands: ```
/conductor start payments --pin v2.3.1 --canary 5 --publish-release
/conductor promote payments --percent 25 --note 'ramping'
/conductor finalize payments --tag 'stable'
/conductor rollback payments --to v2.3.0 --reason 'latency spike' --force
```
Jamie: sample template for release notes? rough: ```
Title: Payments v2.3.1 deploy
Summary: Small perf improvements and fix for currency rounding in edge case
Canary plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 45m
Rollback plan: revert to v2.3.0 using conductor rollback
Impact: risk to payment processing < 0.1% of requests during ramp
Runbook: <link to runbook>
```
Sophie: we should wire conductor to run our eval suite after canary reach threshold and block promotion if regressions found.
Ash: yep — `--post-canary-eval` will be default for payments. failing that, conductor will pause and notify approvers.
release-bot: :white_check_mark: prototype hooks deployed to staging. commands available with prefix `/conductor` in #eng-releases-staging. run `/conductor help` there to test.
Oliver: :thumbsup: quick question — audit logs? should include who pressed the Slack button that triggered finalize/rollback.
Ash: yes, capture `user_id`, `timestamp`, `run_id`, `git-sha` in audit events. store link in thread.
Jamie: next steps: Ash to draft command spec, Alex to add rollback heuristics, Sophie to wire post-canary evals, Oliver to mock Slack modal. I'll collect the spec into a quick RFC later today.
Ash: I'll drop a short `conductor.md` and a Slack modal mock in the staging channel. testing requested from everyone this week.
Sophie: ping me when preflight is in staging, I'll run the test suite.
Alex: I'll sketch the `--safe-rollback` flow and health-check thresholds.
Ash: thanks all. :rocket:
